elements.char: Learning a Variational Network for Reconstruction of Accelerated MRI Data
elements.label: text

elements.char: DISCUSSION
elements.label: formula

elements.char: While deep learning has resulted in clear breakthroughs in Computer Vision, the appli-
elements.label: text

elements.char: cation of deep learning to medical image reconstruction is just beginning (36).
elements.label: text

elements.char: Early
elements.label: text

elements.char: attempts to use machine learning for MRI reconstruction were based on dictionary learn-
elements.label: text

elements.char: ing (37,38). Initial results for our deep learning image reconstruction approach presented
elements.label: text

elements.char: in detail here were first presented at the Annual Meeting of the International Society
elements.label: text

elements.char: for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine in May of 2016 (39). Wang et al. (40) showed first
elements.label: text

elements.char: results using a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to define a relationship
elements.label: text

elements.char: between zero filled solution and high-quality images based on pseudo-random sampling.
elements.label: text

elements.char: The learned network can then be used as regularization in a non-linear reconstruction
elements.label: text

elements.char: algorithm. Yang et al. (41) introduced a network architecture that is based on unrolling
elements.label: text

elements.char: the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers algorithm.
elements.label: text

elements.char: They proposed to learn all
elements.label: text

elements.char: parameters including image transforms and shrinkage functions for CS-based MRI. Han
elements.label: text

elements.char: et al. (42) learned destreaking on CT images and then fine-tuned the learning on MR
elements.label: text

elements.char: data to remove streaking from radially undersampled k-space data. All three approaches
elements.label: text

elements.char: used single-coil data, and it remains unclear how they deal with the complex domain
elements.label: text

elements.char: of MR images.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Kwon et al. (43) introduced a neural network architecture to estimate
elements.label: text

elements.char: the unfolding of multi-coil Cartesian undersampled data.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Similar to a classic SENSE
elements.label: text

elements.char: reconstruction (12), unfolding is performed line-by-line.
elements.label: text

elements.char: This restricts the applicability
elements.label: text

elements.char: to a fixed matrix size and a particular 1D undersampling pattern. Most recently, Lee et
elements.label: text

elements.char: al. (44) used residual learning to train two CNNs to estimate the magnitude and phase
elements.label: text

elements.char: images of Cartesian undersampled data.
elements.label: text

elements.char: In this work, we present the first learning-based MRI reconstruction approach for
elements.label: text

elements.char: clinical multi-coil data.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Our VN architecture combines two fields: variational methods
elements.label: text

elements.char: and deep learning. We formulate image reconstruction as a variational model and embed
elements.label: text

elements.char: this model in a gradient descent scheme, which forms the specific VN structure.
elements.label: text

elements.char: The VN was first introduced as a trainable reaction-diffusion model (6) with applica-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tion to classic image processing tasks (6, 29, 30). All these tasks are similar in the sense
elements.label: text

elements.char: that the data are corrupted by unstructured noise in the image domain. MR image re-
elements.label: text

elements.char: construction presents several substantial differences: complex-valued multi-coil data are
elements.label: text

elements.char: acquired in the Fourier domain and transformed into the image domain. This involves the
elements.label: text

elements.char: use of coil sensitivity maps and causes distinct artifacts related to the sampling pattern.
elements.label: text

elements.char: One of the key strengths of our proposed VN is the motivation by a generalized,
elements.label: text

elements.char: trainable variational model. The solid theoretical foundation of the VN provides insight
elements.label: text

elements.char: into the properties of the learned model. This sets it apart from many learning approaches,
elements.label: text

elements.char: which are essentially treated as black-boxes where it is very challenging to explain the
elements.label: text

elements.char: properties and characteristics of the results. To gain an understanding of what the VN
elements.label: text

elements.char: learns, we first inspect the intermediate outputs of the gradient descent steps of our VN
elements.label: text

elements.char: (see Supporting Video 4).
elements.label: text

elements.char: We observe successive low-pass and high-pass filtering, and
elements.label: text

elements.char: note that the prevalence of undersampling artifacts decreases after each single iteration.
elements.label: text

elements.char: In contrast to iterative reconstruction algorithms, a continuous improvement over the
elements.label: text

elements.char: iterations does not occur because our training is designed such that the result after the
elements.label: text

elements.char: last gradient step is optimal in terms of the error metric chosen for evaluation. Although
elements.label: text

elements.char: it would be possible to train the VN for progressive improvement, this would reduce
